questions.question:
**Select the correct spelling of the underlined word from the given options to make the sentence meaningfully correct.**

I am very __confidant __of my positive result in the examination.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Confident**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Confidant**" refers to a person with whom one shares a secret or private matter.
 
• It is not the appropriate term in this context where the intended meaning is related to self-assurance and certainty about the examination result.
 
• "**Confident**" is an adjective that appropriately describes the speaker's state of mind regarding the positive outcome of the examination.
 
• Therefore, the **corrected sentence** is, "*I am very confident __of my positive result in the examination.*"

Thus, **option 4** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The word "**confidence**" is a noun, while the sentence requires an adjective to describe the speaker's state of mind.
 
• In the context of expressing assurance or certainty about the examination result, an adjective is needed.

questions.solution:

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is* “The travelling gypsies wanted to display __**their skilful antics **__to the crowd”.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Shubhda has not finished __to paint__ the window.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Painting**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The original sentence contains an infinitive ("**to paint**") after "finished," which is not grammatically correct.
 
• In English, it is more natural to use the gerund form in such constructions.
 
• The correct option is "**painting**" because it represents the gerund form of the verb "**paint**."
 
• Verbs like "**finish**," "**complete**," and "**enjoy**" are often followed by **gerunds **when **referring to an activity or action**.
 
• The **corrected sentence** is: "*Shubhda has not finished painting the window.*"
 
• In the sentence, the word "**painting**" acts as a gerund, and it functions as the **object of the verb** "**finished**."
 
• The structure "**finished painting**" indicates that Shubhda did not complete the action of painting the window.

Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the correct pair of homonyms to fill in the blanks.**

What she _______ is that he is a _______ person.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **meant, mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Meant**" is the past tense and past participle of the verb "**mean**," which, in this context, refers to conveying or intending a particular message or idea. (किसी विशेष संदेश या विचार को संप्रेषित या अभिप्रेत करना)
 
• In the sentence, it suggests that the speaker is clarifying or explaining what the woman intended or wanted to express.
 
• "**Mean**," on the other hand, is an adjective that can describe someone as unkind, malicious, or lacking in generosity. (निर्दयी, दुर्भावनापूर्ण, या उदारता की कमी)
 
• In the sentence, it characterizes the person as having a negative or unkind disposition.
 
• The **correct pair of homonyms** to fill in the blanks is: *What she meant __is that he is a __mean __person.*
 
• The sentence conveys the idea that the woman intended to communicate that the person in question has a negative or unkind personality.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
